W5 (contrarian), after E019.
1. Noise. Rebuilding the same commit gives different results. E017 and E019 are both dddcf96 and measured 0.7537 and 0.7541. A rebuild is therefore a small reshuffle, not a fresh draw, which fits H4.3.1. Kernel or graph changes still act like a fresh 3-seed draw: E015, E016 and E017 have the same math and spread 0.7537–0.7607. I put the per-seed SD at about 0.4 pp and the 3-seed SD at about 0.25 pp. My estimate of the tip's true mean is about 0.756, the average of E015/16/17/19 (0.7565) minus a little for winner's curse. The tip's local reading (0.7537) sits about 0.3 pp below its true mean. Any trim costing ≥0.3 pp has roughly even odds of failing the 0.753 bar on a 3-seed draw.
2. Geometry, not pixels. The 2x2 valid stem and three pools give these final-map sizes:
- 32 and 28 px: 3×3
- 24 and 20 px: 2×2

E018 (−0.5 to −0.7 pp after dropping the 28 px phase) and E011 (cliff) fit the idea that what counts is the number of steps run in the 3×3 final-map regime. Prediction: an early 20 px phase replacing 24 px is cheap in accuracy. It runs in the same 2×2 regime, at warm-up or high LR. It also saves less time than people expect, because it only swaps 0.56 for 0.39 cost on 15% of steps (about 3.4%). Untested lever: 26 px (25→12→6→3) replacing 28 px, and 30 px for part of the tail.
3. Time is close to proportional to weighted pixel-MACs. Fixed overhead is ≤0.3 s, and systems levers are exhausted. Conv MACs at 32 px split 20/51/29% across groups 1/2/3. Narrowing group 2 to 320 cuts about 16% of MACs, so I expect about 9–11% less time. Dropping group 1's conv3 cuts about 7% of MACs, plus some memory-bound BN/GELU at the largest maps, so I expect 7–9% less time.
4. Code facts. Muon renormalizes the filters and applies no wd, so filter wd is inert. It runs 3 Newton-Schulz steps. There are 238 true steps (9.5 epochs). The E016 wd effect is mostly noise; E017 gave −0.7 pp on the same math.
5. Accuracy sources:
- averaging: +1 pp (E005)
- Muon at batch 2000: +0.7 pp (E006)
- width: about 0.4 pp per 10% of last-group width (E010)
- steps in the 3×3 regime (E011, E018)

Capacity cuts likely cost more on CIFAR-100 than on CIFAR-10. The 100-class head is width-hungry.
6. The epoch slope at 9.5 epochs is roughly 0.25–0.4 pp per 0.5 epoch (E008-like). Cutting a full epoch likely lands near 0.750.
Unsure: the held-out 10-seed mean from E019's diagnostic (not shown to me), whether the 26 px idea holds, and whether BN recalibration matters (I doubt it).

forecasts.reason: With a true mean of about 0.756 and roughly 0.3 pp lost per 0.5 epoch, cutting 1.0 epoch lands near 0.750, below the bar.
Cuts about 16% of MACs, which buys the ≥5% time, but CIFAR-100 is width-hungry and the 128→320→512 bottleneck likely costs >0.25 pp.
E016's +0.2 pp baseline was a lucky draw; a further wd cut is a reshuffle around a true mean of about 0.756, not +0.2 pp over 0.7607.
Saves about 7–9% of time, short of the 8% bar or near it; the accuracy loss of about 0.4 pp sits right at the hypothesis threshold.
Geometry view: 20 px early is the same 2×2 regime as 24 px, so accuracy is fine, but the weighted-pixel saving is only about 3.4%, below the 4% bar.

cruxes: What is the 10-seed held-out mean from E019's diagnostic? If it is ≥0.757, the margin funds a 0.5-epoch or a group-2 trim; if it is ≤0.755, only time-neutral accuracy gains or geometry-preserving resolution cuts are viable.

Is the accuracy cost of low resolution set by the final-map geometry (3×3 vs 2×2) rather than by pixel count? A 26 px replacement for the 28 px phase would test this cheaply: about 8% less time, ≤0.15 pp lost if true.
Is the accuracy loss per MAC smaller for depth cuts in group 1 or for width cuts in group 2, i.e. which FLOP lever beats the epoch dial at about 2 s per pp?
